title: MLS Goals of the Week: Vintage Lionel Messi, Carlo Holse Heroics
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely12:51 PM EDTLionel Messi (left) gave a vintage performance. / Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Lionel Messi); Bill Barrett/ISI Photos/Getty Images (Carlo Holse)Matchday 29 saw the 2026 MLS season back in full swing as international stars returned to the fold.

There was no shortage of excitement over the weekend, with the Vancouver Whitecaps becoming the first Western Conference team to clinch a playoffs spot and a whole host of comeback victories as Decision Day looms.
Lionel Messi continued his attacking dominance, scoring a brace on Saturday to lift Inter Miami to a dominant 4–0 victory. His latter finish was a vintage, must-see Messi effort.

Meanwhile, St. Louis City’s Carlo Holse had a dazzling performance on Sunday. The winger scored three goals in the span of just 21 minutes, the second-fastest hat trick in MLS history. Thanks to Holse, St. Louis thumped LA Galaxy 6–2 with a whopping five goals in the first half alone. The team is now on a 20-match unbeaten streak, tying the league record.
Here are the top five goals from the weekend.

CARLO HOLSE BAGS HAT TRICK 21 MINUTES INTO THE GAME! 🤯🎩@stlCITYsc fans erupt at Energizer Park. pic.twitter.com/KSZvy9JutX
After scoring in the second and seventh minutes of the game, Holse solidified his hat trick just 14 minutes later.

The 27-year-old attacker settled a launched ball with his chest, before outmuscling Galaxy defender Justin Haak to get the shot off. It signified Holse’s most emphatic display in MLS, and after transfrering to the league in mid-August, he is now up to six goals.
END TO END FOR @OrlandoCitySC and they've surely won it! 🫨Maxime Crépeau save ➡️ Iván Angulo's finish at the end of a beautifully-worked play! pic.twitter.com/FNxTM4YJ4I
The Columbus Crew thought it was about to take a last-gasp lead in the 88th minute, yet just 15 seconds later, Orlando City had reversed fate.

Making the most of Orlando City goalkeeper Maxime Crépeau’s save, the Lions quickly regained possession and sprinted up the pitch into the final third. A quick give-and-go with Martín Ojeda set up  Iván Angulo beautifully in front of the goal mouth for a first-time finish. Orlando walked away with the 3–2 win, leaving the Crew shaking their heads in disbelief.
Kelvin Yeboah gets his 15th of the season!Big response from the Loons to start the second half. 💪📺 Apple TV: https://t.co/4PjpANnTy3 pic.twitter.com/QnmX7hrEjp

It was a willful goal from Minnesota United’s Kelvin Yeboah, who slid into the back post to meet a launched ball from teammate Morris Duggan. His highlight-reel finish equalized the match early in the second half. Another goal from each side would mean the game remained level by the final whistle.
Minnesota will have wanted the win, but it will take the integral point, its first in six games. Yeboah is now up to 15 goals this season.
Messi magic 🪄Two goals for the World Cup Champion. pic.twitter.com/PMA1l5tyZk
In his first outing since his tearful international retirement ceremony with Argentina last week, Messi proved, once again, that he is far from retirement form.

Messi scored twice against DC United, the latter of which saw him skirt three players at the top of the box with his savvy dribbling skill. The emphatic victory was a much-needed confidence boost as it was Inter Miami’s first league win since August.
The Argentine legend is now up to 23 goals this season, increasing his distance in the lead of the thrilling Golden Boot race. FC Dallas’s Petar Musa has the second-most goals with 19.
